title: Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek Release Notes

sections.title: Card Legality
sections.content:
Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek cards with the TRK set code are permitted in the Standard, Pioneer, and Modern formats, as well as in Commander and other formats. At release, the following card sets will be permitted in the Standard format: Magic: The Gathering Foundations, Wilds of Eldraine, The Lost Caverns of Ixalan, Murders at Karlov Manor, Outlaws of Thunder Junction, The Big Score, Bloomburrow, Duskmourn: House of Horror, Aetherdrift, Tarkir: Dragonstorm, Magic: The Gathering— FINAL FANTASY, Edge of Eternities, Magic: The Gathering | Marvel’s Spider-Man, Magic: The Gathering | Avatar: The Last Airbender, Lorwyn Eclipsed, Magic: The Gathering | Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Secrets of Strixhaven, Magic: The Gathering | Marvel Super Heroes, Magic: The Gathering | The Hobbit, Reality Fracture, and Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek. New Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek Commander cards with the TRC set code are permitted in the Commander, Legacy, and Vintage formats. Previously printed cards with the TRC set code are legal for play in any format where a card with the same name is permitted. Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek Stardates cards with the SDS set code are legal for play in any format where a card with the same name is permitted. Go to Magic.Wizards.com/Formats for a complete list of formats and their permitted card sets and banned lists. Go to Magic.Wizards.com/Commander for more information on the Commander variant. Go to Locator.Wizards.com to find an event or store near you.

New Keyword Ability: Beam Me Up

When the away team is in danger, it’s time to engage the transporter and beam them up! Some instant and sorcery cards in this release have the beam me up keyword ability, which allows you to cast them from your graveyard by paying a cost and returning a creature you control to its owner’s hand.

There’s Coffee in that Nebula
{1}{W}
Sorcery
Look at the top five cards of your library. You may reveal a Plains card or nonland permanent card with mana value 3 or less from among them and put it into your hand. Put the rest on the bottom in a random order. Beam me up {2}{W} (You may cast this card from your graveyard for {2}{W} if you also return a creature you control to its owner’s hand. Then exile this spell.)

Energize
{1}{U}
Sorcery
Return target creature an opponent controls to its owner’s hand.
Beam me up {3}{U} (You may cast this card from your graveyard for {3}{U} if you also return a creature you control to its owner’s hand. Then exile this spell.)
• “Beam me up [cost]” means “You may cast this card from your graveyard by paying [cost] and returning a creature you control to its owner’s hand rather than paying its mana cost” and “If the beam me up cost was paid, exile this card instead of putting it anywhere else any time it would leave the stack. ”
• You must still follow any timing restrictions and permissions, including those based on the card’s type. For instance, you can cast a sorcery using beam me up only when you could normally cast a sorcery.
• To determine the total cost of a spell, start with the mana cost or alternative cost (such as a beam me up cost) you’re paying, add any cost increases, then apply any cost reductions. The mana value of the spell is determined only by its mana cost, no matter what the total cost to cast the spell was.
• A spell cast using beam me up will always be exiled afterward, whether it resolves, is countered, or leaves the stack in some other way.
• You can cast a spell using beam me up even if it was somehow put into your graveyard without having been cast.
• If a card with beam me up is put into your graveyard during your turn, you can cast it if it’s legal to do so before any other player can take any actions.

New Keyword Action: Assimilate

An encounter with the Borg comes with two guarantees: You will be assimilated , and resistance is futile. The assimilate keyword action gives you control of a creature or puts a creature card onto the battlefield under your control. Either way, a +1/+1 counter is put on that creature, and it becomes a Borg artifact creature and loses its other creature types.

Death Is Irrelevant
{6}{B}{B}
Enchantment
Artifact creatures you control have indestructible.
At the beginning of your end step, assimilate target creature card from a graveyard. (Put it onto the battlefield under your control with a +1/+1 counter. It’s a Borg artifact creature and loses all other creature types.)

The Best of Both Worlds
{4}{W}{U}
Enchantment — Saga
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Assimilate target nonartifact creature an opponent controls. (Gain control of it and put a +1/+1 counter on it. It’s a Borg artifact creature and loses all other creature types.)
II — Artifact creatures you control get +2/+2 until end of turn.
III — Exile the Borg assimilated with this Saga, then return it to the battlefield under its owner’s control.
• The assimilated creature or creature card loses any other creature types it has, but it keeps any other supertypes, types, and subtypes it has. For example, if a Dryad Arbor (a Land Creature – Forest Dryad) is assimilated, it will be an Artifact Land Creature – Forest Borg.
New Term: Face a Dilemma
Starfleet officers are presented with a lot of tough decisions, and if you think you’ve got what it takes to make those calls, we’ve got the mechanic for you. Some cards in this release have abilities that trigger whenever a player “faces a dilemma,” which happens whenever that player chooses one or more modes for a spell or ability.

Elim Garak, Simple Tailor
{2}{B}
Legendary Creature — Cardassian Rogue
3/3
Menace
Whenever you face a dilemma, each opponent loses 2 life and you gain 2 life. (You face a dilemma as you choose one or more modes for a spell or ability.)

Jett Reno, Problem Solver
{1}{U}
Legendary Creature — Human Artificer
1/2
Whenever Jett Reno, becomes tapped, surveil 1. If her power is 4 or greater, instead draw a card.
Whenever you face a dilemma, put a +1/+1 counter on Jett Reno. (You face a dilemma as you choose one or more modes for a spell or ability.)
• A spell or ability is modal if it has two or more options in a bulleted list and instructions for a player to choose a number of those options, such as “Choose one” or “Choose one or more.” Each of those options is a mode. Spells with spree or tiered are modal spells.
• Modal spells and cards with modal abilities printed prior to the Khans of Tarkir release didn’t use bulleted lists for the modes; these cards have received errata in the Oracle card reference.
• As long as you choose one or more modes for a spell or ability, you’ve faced a dilemma. It doesn’t matter if that spell or ability goes on to resolve or not.
• An ability that triggers whenever a player faces a dilemma will resolve before the spell or ability that caused it to trigger. It resolves even if that spell or ability is countered or otherwise leaves the stack without resolving.
• If a player chooses more than one mode for a spell or ability, that player still faced only one dilemma.
• If a player chooses no modes for a spell or ability, the player did not face a dilemma . This can happen because the instruction to choose modes for the spell or ability is optional (“You may choose one,” or similar) or because there are no legal modes to choose for a modal triggered ability.

sections.title: New Ability Word: Federation
sections.content:
The Federation brings together a large number of member worlds and their inhabitants, and that diversity is one of the Federation’s greatest strengths. The federation ability word groups abilities that care about the number of creature types among non-Borg creatures a player controls.

Starfleet Academy
Legendary Land
{T}: Add {C}.
Federation — {5}, {T}: Choose a color. Add an amount of mana of that color equal to the number of creature types among non-Borg creatures you control.
• Don’t consider Borg creatures at all when counting creature types for federation abilities, even if they have additional creature types. However, a Borg having another creature type doesn’t mean that type can’t be counted, as long as a non-Borg also has it. For example, if you control a Borg Noble and a Human Noble, the number of creature types among non-Borg creatures you control is two (Human and Noble).

sections.title: New Ability Word: Strange New Worlds
sections.content:
Exploring unknown planets is part of Starfleet’s mission, and you can be part of that effort. The strange new worlds ability word groups abilities that care about the number of differently named lands you control.

sections.title: New Ability Word: Battlefront
sections.content:
The Klingon Empire is known for its military power, and with this release, you can bring that power to bear against your opponents. The Klingon appreciation for combat is reflected here in the battlefront ability word, which groups abilities that care about the number of opponents you attacked this turn.

Martok, Hero of the Empire
{2}{W}
Legendary Creature — Klingon Warrior
2/2
Battlefront — Whenever you attack, put a +1/+1 counter on each of up to X target creatures you control, where X is the number of opponents you attacked this turn.

Own the Day
{4}{R}{R}
Sorcery
Battlefront — This spell costs {1} less to cast for each opponent you attacked this turn.
Untap all creatures that attacked this turn. After this main phase, there is an additional combat phase followed by an additional main phase.
• Opponents you attacked this turn that left the game later in the turn are still counted by battlefront abilities. For example, if you attack three opponents and one of them loses the game as a result, then you cast Own the Day during your second main phase, it will cost {3} less to cast.
• Battlefront abilities won’t count an opponent if you attacked only planeswalkers that player controlled and/or battles that player protected and not the player themself.

sections.title: New Ability Word: Seek Out
sections.content:
Hoping to search uncharted space for new life and new civilizations but don’t have time for a five-year mission? Well, you never know what you’ll find if you just keep drawing cards! This spirit of discovery is represented by the seek out ability word, which groups abilities that trigger whenever you draw your second card each turn.

Beverly Crusher, Ship’s Doctor
{2}{W}
Legendary Creature — Human Doctor
2/2
Seek out — Whenever you draw your second card each turn, put a +1/+1 counter on each of up to three target creatures.

Rom and Leeta, Unlikely Pair
{3}{R}
Legendary Creature — Ferengi Bajoran
4/3
Seek out — Whenever you draw your second card each turn, create two tapped Treasure tokens.
• A permanent with a seek out ability doesn’t need to have been under your control when the first card is drawn for its ability to trigger. As long as you control it when you draw your second card in a turn, that ability will trigger.

sections.title: Returning Ability Word: Landfall
sections.content:
In yet another reflection of the theme of exploration, the landfall ability returns in this release. It groups abilities that reward you whenever a land you control enters.

Planetary Patrol
{1}{R}
Creature — Scout
2/2
Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, this creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.

Jake Sisko, War Correspondent
{1}{G}
Legendary Creature — Human Citizen
2/2
Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, you gain 1 life. If this is the second time this ability has resolved this turn, investigate. (Create a Clue token. It’s an artifact with “{2}, Sacrifice this token: Draw a card.”)
• A landfall ability triggers whenever a land you control enters for any reason. It triggers whenever you play a land, as well as whenever a spell or ability puts a land onto the battlefield under your control.
• A landfall ability doesn’t trigger if a permanent already on the battlefield becomes a land.
• Whenever a land you control enters, each landfall ability of permanents you control will trigger. You can put them on the stack in any order. The last ability you put on the stack will be the first one to resolve (as a result, you can have those abilities resolve in the order of your choosing).
Returning Land Type: Planet
Where can you find all that new life and those new civilizations? Well, good news: we’ve brought the Planet land type back so you know where to look.

Earth, Sector 001
Land — Planet
This land enters tapped.
When this land enters, you gain 1 life. {T}: Add {G} or {U}.

Qo’noS
Land — Planet
This land enters tapped.
When this land enters, you gain 1 life. {T}: Add {B} or {R}.
• Planet is a land subtype with no special meaning. It doesn’t grant the land any intrinsic abilities.

sections.title: Returning Keyword: Station
sections.content:
Returning Artifact Type: Spacecraft If you’ve ever wanted to captain a Federation starship, a Klingon battle cruiser, or even a Borg cube, here’s your chance. The station mechanic is back to help you get your Spacecraft up and running; once they’ve got the right amount of charge counters, they’ll be ready to use all their abilities. In most cases, this will also turn them into creatures ready to attack and block. U.S.S. Enterprise-A, Free Spirit {3}{W}{W} Legendary Artifact — Spacecraft 5/5 Ward {2} When U.S.S. Enterprise-A enters, create three 1/1 red Officer creature tokens. Station (Tap another creature you control: Put charge counters equal to its power on this Spacecraft. Station only as a sorcery. It’s an artifact creature at 6+.) 6+ | Flying, lifelink

Romulan Bird-of-Prey
{1}{U}
Artifact — Spacecraft
4/4
Cloaking Device — As long as this Spacecraft isn’t a creature, it has hexproof.
Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, if this Spacecraft isn’t a creature, put two charge counters on it. Station 8+ | Flying
• Spacecraft is an artifact type with no special meaning. It doesn’t grant the artifact any intrinsic abilities. Other cards may care about which artifacts are Spacecraft.
• A station card is a card with the station keyword ability. The station keyword means “Tap another untapped creature you control: Put a number of charge counters on this permanent equal to the tapped creature ’s power. Activate only as a sorcery.”
• Use the tapped creature’s power as the station ability resolves to determine how many charge counters to put on the permanent with station. If that creature isn’t on the battlefield at that time, use its power as it last existed on the battlefield.
• If the tapped creature has negative power, no charge counters are put onto or removed from the permanent with station.
• Each station card has one or more striations in its text box. Each striation is preceded by a station symbol — a circle surrounding a number and a plus sign.
• Each station symbol represents an ability. A station symbol means “As long as this permanent has N or more charge counters on it, it has [abilities],” where N is the number inside the symbol and [abilities] are all the abilities found inside the same striation as that symbol.
• If that station symbol is in the same striation as a power and toughness box, it instead means “As long as this permanent has N or more charge counters on it, it has [abilities] and is a creature with base power and toughness [P/T] in addition to its other types.”
• If a station card has a power and toughness box printed in one of the striations in its text box, it ’s not a creature unless it has the appropriate number of charge counters on it. That card also doesn ’t have that power and toughness in any zone other than the battlefield.
• If an effect causes a permanent with station to become a creature by some means other than having the appropriate number of charge counters on it, it won’t use any power and toughness values printed in its text box. Instead, it will use whatever base power and toughness was set by the effect that made it a creature.
• If another permanent becomes a copy of a permanent represented by a station card, all of its printed abilities, including the ones represented by station symbols, are copied. Its current characteristics and the number of charge counters on it are not copied. The abilities (and in some cases, types, power, and toughness) are determined based on the number of charge counters on the copy.
• The abilities of a permanent with station are based on the number of charge counters it has. This means that if a permanent with station gets charge counters due to some other effect (such as proliferate) or loses charge counters somehow, its abilities change accordingly. The same is true for determining whether that permanent is a creature.
• Even if a permanent with station has equal or greater charge counters than the number in its last station symbol, you can still activate its station ability. Adding more charge counters won’t give it additional abilities, but other effects or cards might make those extra counters relevant.
• If a permanent with station becomes a creature, it will be able to attack if it’s been under your control continuously since the turn began. That is, it doesn’t matter how long it’s been a creature, just how long it’s been on the battlefield.

If you reveal a nonland card this way, you won’t put a +1/+1 counter on anything, but you may put the revealed card into your graveyard. Effects that trigger “whenever a creature explores” trigger as appropriate.
